title: Hokkaido is a Switch 2 emulator for Android that now also offers native ports
summary: Emulation or native port? This updated emulator doesn't force you to choose.
body: Credit: Oliver Cragg / Android Authority TL;DR The Hokkaido emulator for running Switch 2 games on Android now has built-in Banana Native support. This means you can generate and play native ports of Switch 2 titles via the emulator. Switch 2 emulation and ports require an Android device with high-end silicon and plenty of RAM, though. The Nintendo Switch 2 only launched last year, but we’ve recently seen the first emulators arriving on Android, along with native game ports. Now, one of these emulators will also allow you to play native ports. Hokkaido version 0.7.0 was released on GitHub and this emulator now lets you generate and play native ports of select Switch 2 games thanks to the integrated Banana Native tool. The port is generated entirely within the emulator’s UI.

title: Google Voice on Android gets redesign, hints at future RCS support
summary: Google Voice is finally getting a fresh coat of paint.
body: TL;DR Google is rolling out a redesign of the Google Voice app on Android. The new look borrows heavily from Google Messages, including a rounded text field and an “SMS” label on the send button. The redesign also hints that RCS support could be coming to Google Voice soon. Google Voice has been getting some much-needed attention lately. We recently found evidence of RCS support in an app teardown, and shortly after, we saw a redesign appear in its web app interface . That redesign also showed new service indicators — SMS or MMS — which could be in preparation for RCS support. Now, that redesign is rolling out to the Google Voice Android app as well, as spotted by 9to5Google . The redesign is reportedly rolling out in the latest version of the Google Voice app (v019342246) and looks clearly inspired by Google Messages. There’s a rounded text field at the bottom with attachment and camera icons. There’s also a new long-press gesture that opens up a context menu, similar to Google Messages.

title: Google now lets Gemini users opt out of AI training while keeping their chat history
summary: You can now keep your Gemini chat history while opting out of data training.
body: Credit: Megan Ellis / Android Authority TL;DR The Gemini app is getting new settings that allow you to keep your chat history while opting out of AI training. If history is turned off, your chats will now be saved for around two months. This will be a global update that arrives in the coming weeks. While not always the case, when you use AI, it’s fairly safe to assume that companies are using your data to train their models. It’s the trade-off you often have to be comfortable with if you want to use these products. However, Google is now updating the Gemini app to give users a new option. In a brief blog post , Google announced it is giving you more control over when your Gemini chat history is used for generative AI training. The update will introduce new settings that will let you opt out of training while keeping your chat history. Additionally, you’ll still be able to control how long your history is stored and review or delete history manually.

title: Google Vids now lets you create a personal avatar at no cost

body: Credit: Google TL;DR Google is expanding personal avatars to users with personal Google accounts. Personal avatar lets you create a custom AI-generated avatar. Avatars are linked to your account and are restricted to the account holder’s likeness. Back in March, we spotted that Google was working on a feature that would allow you to turn your likeness into a virtual avatar. That feature would eventually be known as Gemini avatar and later rolled out for Google Vids as personal avatar. While the feature was previously behind a paywall, that’s no longer the case. Google initially announced the plan to roll out custom avatars for Workspace users with personal accounts at the beginning of November. However, a day after the announcement, the company decided to delay the rollout. No explanation was given for the pause, and the tech giant did not offer a resume date. Fast forward to today, personal avatars are now available for personal Google accounts for free.

title: Pixel owners are seeing a weird animation bug when closing recent apps
summary: A ghosting bug is making Android’s smooth app-closing animation look broken.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Some Pixel owners are experiencing a glitch with the recent apps screen. Visual ghosting occurs when swiping up to close an app. Users say that the visual bug started happening after the October update. Android has some pretty smooth animations, from the shrinking transition you see when exiting an app to the subtle bounce when opening Quick Settings . The animations are so smooth that some people may not even notice them. That’s why when the fluidity of these animations breaks, it stands out like a sore thumb. Unfortunately, it appears a bug is doing just that when closing out of apps. Some Pixel owners are experiencing a visual glitch when trying to close an app via the recent apps screen. To close an app on the recent apps screen, you can either swipe up on the app or scroll all the way to the left and hit the Clear all button. According to reports , swiping up on an app causes a trail (visual ghosting) to appear instead of the smooth animation that should happen.

body: TL;DR Google is introducing Gemini Channels to remotely interact with the AI service. Users can set up Channels over both text messaging and email. Google already gives us a million and one different way to access Gemini through apps , web interfaces, and more, and now it looks like we’re getting a new option for remotely interacting with Gemini, as Google introduces Channels for text messages. We first noticed noted Google preparing to add this new Channels option in Gemini settings, but it wasn’t immediately clear what it was for. It led us to gemini.google.com/channels , which at the time just redirected to the main Gemini page. But today it looks like Google has finally flipped the switch on this live, and we can now see it for what it is: a way to interact with Gemini over text or email (Thanks: Joshua).

title: Apple’s buggy HomeView launch is making Google Home look good
summary: Some HomeView buyers are already returning their units over buggy Siri AI.
body: TL;DR Early Apple HomeView buyers are returning their $299 smart displays due to buggy software, unreliable Siri AI, and setup failures. Even prominent tech reviewers have criticized the experience, describing it as beta-like. Apple has promised a December update to address some Siri AI shortcomings. Apple took its time entering the smart display market, giving Google years to establish itself in kitchens, bedrooms, and living rooms. But if the first few days of the Apple HomeView are any indication, Google may have less reason to worry about its new rival than we initially thought. Some early buyers are already packing up their $299 smart displays and sending them back to Apple. The HomeView, which went on sale on November 13, has earned plenty of praise for its hardware . Unfortunately, the software meant to bring that hardware to life is proving to be its biggest weakness. Siri AI, whose delayed arrival reportedly held up the HomeView’s launch, is struggling with the very tasks that make a smart display worth having.

summary: Google wants Gemini to sound more like the people you talk to every day.
body: TL;DR Google is rolling out 66 new regional voices to the Gemini app on Android and iOS. The expansion covers seven language variants, including US English, with more than 10 voices available for UK English alone. Your chosen voice applies to both Gemini Live conversations and spoken responses in regular chats. When Amazon-owned Ring wanted its video doorbells to feel a little more familiar to customers in Scotland, it launched a nationwide search for someone to record greetings in a Scottish accent. The idea was simple: hearing a familiar voice when you interact with technology can make the experience feel more personal. Google is now bringing that same idea to Gemini , only this time, you’ll be able to hold an entire conversation with an AI that speaks with a local accent. Google first teased regional voices for Gemini at I/O in May, and the company is now rolling out 66 new voice options to the Gemini app on Android and iOS. These cover seven language variants: US English, UK English, Indian English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Korean.
